item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 242336
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
800 PM EDT Thu Sep 24 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Fay, located several hundred miles southwest of the Azores.

Far Eastern Tropical Atlantic (AL90):
Recent satellite-derived wind data indicates that an area of low
pressure located less than 200 miles to the south-southeast of the
Cabo Verde Islands is producing winds of 40-45 mph to the north of
its center, which is gradually becoming better defined. In addition,
the system is producing a large area of showers and thunderstorms
that are also showing signs of organization. If these current trends
continue, the system is likely to become a short-lived tropical
storm as soon as later tonight or on Friday while it moves
northwestward to northward. Increasing upper-level winds, however,
should prevent further development over the weekend. Interests in
the Cabo Verde Islands should monitor the progress of this system as
gusty winds, areas of heavy rain, and flash flooding are possible
over the islands by Friday. Heavy rain and flash flooding could
also occur well to the east along the coast of western Africa,
particularly in western portions of Senegal, The Gambia,
Guinea-Bissau, and southwest portions of Mauritania.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...80 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...80 percent.

$$
Forecaster Papin

LOCATION...29.8N 42.3W

PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 270 DEGREES AT 6 MPH...9 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1005 MB...29.68 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 300 AM GMT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Fay was
located near latitude 29.8 North, longitude 42.3 West. Fay is moving
toward the west near 6 mph (9 km/h), and is expected to shift 
west-southwest over the next 24 hours.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 50 mph (85 km/h) with higher gusts.
Some slight additional strengthening is possible over the next 12 
hours. Thereafter, gradual weakening is expected through the 
weekend.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 80 miles (130 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1005 mb (29.68 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------

$$
Forecaster Evans/Kelly

item.title: Tropical Storm Fay Forecast Discussion Number 20
item.description:
Issued at 300 AM GMT Fri Sep 25 2026 
000
WTNT41 KNHC 250249
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Storm Fay Discussion Number  20
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
300 AM GMT Fri Sep 25 2026

Fay has developed a more consistent area of deep convection about 
its center since the last advisory. Little has changed with the 
subjective and objective satellite intensity estimates of this 
storm, however. CIMSS-UW objective estimates range from 35 to 45 
kt, while TAFB rated Fay at 3.0 or 45 kt. Because of this, Fay's 
initial intensity has been held steady at 45 kt. 

The initial motion remains at 270/5 kt. Fay's forward motion is 
expected to remain slow as its steering environment is 
characterized by weak easterly winds within the Atlantic 
subtropical high. Over the next 24 h, Fay is expected to shift 
west-southwest and then southwest as high pressure amplifies to its 
west. At the same time, Fay's speed is expected to decrease even 
further. The latest track forecast reflects this trend toward the 
southwest, and closely follows HCCA guidance. 

With convection deepening on satellite imagery, Fay could 
experience a brief increase in intensity overnight, before steady 
weakening is forecast as the storm experiences increasingly drier 
mid-level air and vertical wind shear. While global forecast models 
suggest that Fay will lose its convection over the weekend, its 
closed circulation may persist into the middle of next week, 
allowing Fay to remain a post-tropical remnant low during that 
time. The main change for the latest forecast was to reflect a later 
dissipation time, but otherwise Fay's overall trend remains the 
same.

item.title: Tropical Storm Gonzalo Public Advisory Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM CVT Fri Sep 25 2026 
659 
WTNT32 KNHC 250245
TCPAT2
 
BULLETIN
Tropical Storm Gonzalo Advisory Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL072026
200 AM CVT Fri Sep 25 2026
 
...TROPICAL STORM GONZALO FORMS SOUTH-SOUTHEAST OF THE CABO VERDE
ISLANDS...
...TROPICAL STORM WARNING ISSUED FOR THE CABO VERDE ISLANDS...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM CVT...0300 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...13.2N 22.1W
ABOUT 190 MI...305 KM SE OF THE SOUTHERNMOST CABO VERDE ISLANDS
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...45 MPH...75 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NNW OR 330 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1004 MB...29.65 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
CHANGES WITH THIS ADVISORY:
 
The Government of the Cabo Verde Islands has issued a Tropical
Storm Warning for all of the Cabo Verde Islands.
 
SUMMARY OF WATCHES AND WARNINGS IN EFFECT:
 
A Tropical Storm Warning is in effect for...
* The Cabo Verde Islands.
 
A Tropical Storm Warning means that tropical storm conditions are
expected somewhere within the warning area, in this case within 24
hours.
 
For storm information specific to your area, please monitor
products issued by your national meteorological service.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM CVT (0300 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Gonzalo was
located near latitude 13.2 North, longitude 22.1 West. Gonzalo is
moving toward the north-northwest near 8 mph (13 km/h), and this
motion is expected to continue over the next several days, with a
slower forward speed this weekend. On the forecast track, the center
will pass near or over portions of the Cabo Verde Islands today and
tonight.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 45 mph (75 km/h) with higher gusts. 
Some strengthening is possible today, with a gradual weakening trend 
forecast to begin this weekend.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 175 miles (280 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1004 mb (29.65 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
Key messages for Gonzalo can be found in the Tropical Cyclone
Discussion under AWIPS header MIATCDAT2 and WMO header WTNT42 KNHC.
 
WIND: Tropical storm conditions are expected to reach the Cabo Verde
Islands within the warning area later this morning.
 
RAINFALL: Tropical Storm Gonzalo is expected to produce rainfall
totals of 1 to 3 inches – 30 to 75 mm — across the eastern portions
of the Cabo Verde Islands on Friday and Saturday with less than 1
inch anticipated for the western side of the island chain. Heavy
rain along the coastal areas of Guinea-Bissau, The Gambia, and 
Senegal will produce totals between 2 to 4 inches – 50 to 100 mm – 
with isolated higher amounts along the immediate coast.
 
SURF: Swells generated by the storm are expected to affect the Cabo
Verde Islands through Saturday. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next intermediate advisory at 500 AM CVT.
Next complete advisory at 800 AM CVT.
 
$$
Forecaster Kelly
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Tropical Storm Gonzalo Forecast Discussion Number 1
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM CVT Fri Sep 25 2026 
303 
WTNT42 KNHC 250246
TCDAT2
 
Tropical Storm Gonzalo Discussion Number   1
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL072026
200 AM CVT Fri Sep 25 2026
 
Satellite imagery indicates that the area of low pressure (Invest
AL90) has developed a closed, albeit slightly elongated, low-level
circulation this morning along with organized deep convection. 
This convection is currently displaced mainly over the eastern and
southern semicircles of the circulation due to moderate westerly 
vertical wind shear. Recent scatterometer data show maximum winds 
near 40 kt in the northeastern quadrant, and TAFB provided a 
subjective Dvorak satellite intensity estimate of T2.5/35 kt. Based 
on these data, advisories are being initiated on Tropical Storm 
Gonzalo with an initial intensity of 40 kt. A Tropical Storm Warning 
has been issued for all the Cabo Verde Islands.
 
The initial motion is somewhat uncertain given the recent formation
of the center, but the best estimate is 330/7 kt. Gonzalo is
expected to move north-northwestward during the next couple of days,
steered by the flow of a deep mid-level trough over the eastern
Atlantic. As this trough lifts northeastward later in the forecast
period, the cyclone will be left behind in a very weak steering
environment, causing it to drift slowly over the eastern Atlantic.
On the forecast track, the center will pass near or over portions of
the Cabo Verde Islands today and tonight. Track guidance is in
fairly good agreement in the short term, though cross- and
along-track differences emerge beyond day 2. The official NHC track
forecast lies near the HCCA corrected consensus and the TVCN simple
consensus aids.
 
Gonzalo is currently located within a marginally conducive
environment that could allow for some slight strengthening,
characterized by sea surface temperatures near 27-28C and mid-level
relative humidity values around 60 percent. In about 24 hours,
vertical wind shear is forecast to increase to moderate-to-strong 
levels. This increase in shear, combined with cooling SSTs and a
progressively drier mid-level environment, will cause a gradual
weakening trend. The NHC intensity forecast lies near the HCCA
corrected consensus aid. Global model simulated infrared satellite
imagery depicts Gonzalo losing organized deep convection in about 3
days, and the forecast shows the system becoming a post-tropical
remnant low at that time, and remaining a remnant low through the
remainder of the forecast period.
 
Key Messages:
 
1. Tropical storm conditions are expected to spread across portions
of the Cabo Verde Islands, where a Tropical Storm Warning is in 
effect, later today and will continue through tonight.
 
2. Heavy rains from Gonzalo could affect the eastern islands of Cabo 
Verde and the western coast of Africa between Guinea-Bissau to 
Senegal today through Saturday. Areas of flash flooding will be 
possible along the western coast of Africa with some isolated flash 
flood concerns for the eastern islands of Cabo Verde.
